10.1002_adma.75561: The performance enhancement of emerging flexible batteries relies on the development of advanced small‐particle electrode materials. However, current cathode materials with reduced particle size mostly suffer from low operating voltage, especially aqueous based electrodes. In this study, by using laser‐induced carbothermal method, we successfully fabricated high‐entropy doped Li‐rich nanoparticles as layered oxide cathodes that exhibit outstanding high‐voltage performances. The direct bottom–up nanocrystal growth enables the formation of such exclusive Li‐rich nanoparticles with unprecedentedly small diameter of 83.08 nm. As confirmed by atomic‐resolution imaging, operando x‐ray diffraction and synchrotron techniques analysis, the cathode achieves high lattice stability at elevated cut‐off voltage through the combined effects of heteroatomic composition and reduced particle diameters. Molecular dynamics simulations using machine‐learning interatomic potentials further demonstrate suppressed oxygen loss and stabilized transition‐metal framework in the high‐entropy doped cathodes. Consequently, the cathode operates steadily at voltage window of 2.5–4.8 V with ultrahigh power density of 877.9 Wh kg −1 at 1 C. The assembled full cell and fiber battery provide significant practical feasibility during high‐voltage cycling. This work provides an efficient strategy for designing high‐voltage flexible batteries, offering critical insights for next‐generation energy storage research.
10.1002_cssc.202501807: Electrosynthesis of ammonia (NH 3 ) with renewable energy sources offers a highly promising alternative for sustainable NH 3 production under mild conditions. Among the reported NH 3 synthesis catalysts, single‐atom catalysts display high activity, selectivity, and stability toward NH 3 synthesis reactions owing to their well‐defined catalytic sites and maximum metal‐atom utilization. Conjugated coordination polymers (CCPs) with single‐atom active sites and precisely controlled coordination environment hold significant potential in electrochemical NH 3 synthesis. Abundant advances have been recently made toward the development of CCPs for NH 3 synthesis at ambient conditions. This review specifically discusses several strategies of CCPs modification and their applications in the synthesis of NH 3 . Finally, the existing challenges are discussed and perspectives on future developments are provided.
10.1016_j.fuel.2026.138961: Combined-cycle gas turbines (CCGT) traditionally provide electrical power and heat for district heating, playing a key role in ensuring operational resilience and security of energy supply, but they are associated with significant CO 2 emissions. This paper investigates a retrofit concept based on oxy-fuel combustion and water electrolysis that enables decoupling of heat, electricity, H 2 , and CO 2 production within an existing CCGT. A detailed AspenPlus model of a real Finnish 1010 MW th CCGT is developed for both air-fired and oxy-fuel configurations. At the same turbine inlet temperature, oxy-fuel combustion decreased the power output from 164 to 141 MW e per gas turbine due to the change in working-fluid properties while increasing the heat for district heating (22 to 95 MW th ). Dry steam injection at the turbine inlet improved performance by lowering turbine inlet temperature, reducing CO 2 recirculation need, and increasing turbine power while decreasing compressor power demand. Subcooled water injection shifted the system toward enhanced heat recovery. The electricity required to produce O 2 for oxy-fuel combustion exceeded the CCGT output but could be supplied from the grid. The electrolysis system produced 10.2 kg/s of H 2 , and the non-recirculated flue gas contained 98.0 mol % CO 2 . Hydrogen co-firing increased the heat and power generation, the electrical efficiency of the oxy-fuel cycle, and the district heating supply temperature without requiring live steam from the steam cycle as in the air-fired configuration. Beyond emission reduction, the proposed oxy-fuel CCGT enables flexible operation through hydrogen co-firing, sustaining district heating while interacting with the electricity grid, thereby enhancing system flexibility and resilience under high renewable penetration. • Detailed AspenPlus model evaluates dry, steam, and water-injected oxy-fuel cycles. • Dry steam injection effectively increases the efficiency of the oxy-fuel cycle. • Oxy-fuel combustion in gas turbines enables flexible operation between heat and power. • H 2 co-firing enables district heating supply temperatures up to 125 ∘ C. • Turbomachinery geometry redesign is required for oxy-fuel retrofitting.
